description: Subset-based F2 dynamic program with first-hull-gap recurrence completion for a bounded fixed-point hull-order TSP profile.

source.title: The Traveling Salesman Problem with Few Inner Points
source.reference: Section 4; Encyclopedia of Algorithms, Chapter 426, DOI 10.1007/978-1-4939-2864-4_426
source.algorithm_attribution: second fixed-parameter algorithm: subset recurrence F2[i,S,r] over the outer prefix and interior subsets, with the i=1 inner transition completed to include the first hull gap
source.implementation_status: bounded clean-room algorithm implementation; no source code, prose, figures, or test data copied

input.encoding: [n,k,outer IDs in supplied cyclic hull order,inner IDs,x0,y0,...,x(n-1),y(n-1)]
input.point_constraint: All coordinates are distinct; outer IDs are the strict convex hull in cyclic order and inner IDs are strictly interior. The geometric classification is supplied, as assumed by the source algorithm.

output.definition: Minimum fixed-point cost among closed tours respecting the supplied cyclic hull order, with each Euclidean edge rounded to the nearest thousandth (halfway cases downward); this bounded rounded-metric hull-order profile does not claim the unrestricted exact-Euclidean optimum

workspace.meaning: Two rolling subset-DP rows, bounded point coordinates, and fixed-point distance scratch.

contract.outer_order: Use the supplied hull cycle exactly; either orientation and any starting hull vertex are accepted.
contract.subset_state: F2[i,S,r] is the minimum path cost on the first i outer vertices and interior subset S, ending at r in S or at the current outer vertex.
contract.subset_order: Interior subset states are processed by increasing bitmask; each transition adds one missing interior-point bit.
contract.first_gap_completion: Seed the first outer vertex with the empty subset and apply the inner-point transition before advancing to the second outer vertex, allowing interior points in the first hull gap.
contract.distance_rounding: For squared integer distance s, compute the nearest integer to sqrt(s*1000^2), rounding an exact tie downward, using integer arithmetic.
